extracted.intended_audience: researchers, research-integrity professionals, and readers interested in scientific publishing and retractions
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and describe factors that lead to a paper's retraction (misconduct, missing data, irreproducibility, figure manipulation, institutional actions) as illustrated by this Retraction Watch report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data fabrication and manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inappropriate manipulation and fabrication of data by the first author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The retraction notice states the paper is being retracted due to 'inappropriate manipulation and fabrication of data' by the first author; manipulation of data within figures (e.g., bar graphs) is cited specifically as affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorrect conclusions resulting from misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Misconduct led to an incorrect conclusion in the paper (example: that NADPH activity is elevated in Huntington’s disease).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When alleged misconduct produces an incorrect scientific conclusion, that incorrect inference is a stated grounds for retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing original data
rubrics_metrics.description: Some original data supporting the paper were missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice reports missing original data as part of the basis for retraction; absence of primary data undermines ability to verify results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to replicate findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts to replicate findings using the reported method or an alternative approach were unsuccessful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsuccessful replication attempts (both via reported method and alternative approaches) are cited as evidence that the results are not reliable and support retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure/graph integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged manipulation and fabrication affected bar graphs in two of the paper's figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific tampering with graphical elements (e.g., bar graphs, images) is highlighted as a concrete indicator of data manipulation and a reason to retract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional review and panel endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: An institutional faculty panel supports the decision and the stated reasons for the retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional investigations and panels that review allegations and endorse retraction decisions are an important procedural element; institutions typically follow federal regulations and their own policies in handling these matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding author/institutional action in retraction process
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding author is the party retracting the paper; institutional spokespeople may comment (or decline) while following policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retractions may be issued by corresponding authors; institutions may limit public comment ('we typically do not comment on these situations') while indicating they take integrity concerns seriously and follow required procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of related publications for comparable issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and journals may check other publications by the same authors for similar problems (example: a follow-up JHD paper was double-checked and found to have no comparable issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an author is implicated in misconduct, journals often review their other work; a lack of comparable issues in other papers is relevant to scope of the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for researcher profile and employment visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional removal of researcher profiles and changes in reported employment may follow allegations (MGH removed Valencia’s Research Investigator Profile; LinkedIn lists new employer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal of institutional web profiles and alterations in public employment listings are observable consequences that may accompany misconduct allegations or departures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and impact considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The study's citation record (e.g., cited 53 times per Web of Science) is noted when assessing the reach/impact of a retracted paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number of citations and downstream use of the paper are relevant when evaluating the significance and potential harm of a retracted work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of the retraction notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A published retraction notice that states the reasons and basis for retraction (date and explanatory text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article references a retraction notice (published Aug. 22) that explains the reasons; clear notices that state the factual basis for retraction help the community understand what went wrong.
